btc_link.lede: Neutral for BTC: from where the S&P is now, BTC's next 30 days have been about normal, so the S&P is not giving a clear early sign either way.
lines: Where the S&P is: 7,183 on 25 Nov 2026, -8.1% from its 1-year closing high, below its 50D (7,603) and below its 200D (7,352): Risk-off.

What BTC did next from here: since 2015, on S&P days like this (with the BTC–S&P link at 0.3 or more), BTC's next 30 days were +2.7% (median), up 59% of the time, with a 10%+ drop at some point in 35% (all days: +2.9%, 57% up, 35%; 337 days).

How closely BTC follows: the 60-day correlation is 0.65 (high; higher than 99% of days since 2015), so S&P down days are BTC down days right now. The S&P does not lead BTC by a day; the link is same-day.

Live early signs: S&P closes 5%+ below its 20-day closing high (5 Nov 2026, 14 trading days ago): after the 25 past cases BTC's next 30 days were +2.1% (median), with a 10%+ drop in 44% (all days 35%); BTC -20.4% since. S&P falls 2% or more in one day (19 Nov 2026, 4 trading days ago): after the 52 past cases BTC's next 30 days were +4.0% (median), with a 10%+ drop in 37% (all days 35%); BTC -2.5% since. S&P closes below its 200D (17 Nov 2026, 6 trading days ago): after the 15 past cases BTC's next 30 days were +8.6% (median), with a 10%+ drop in 13% (all days 35%); BTC -6.9% since.

btc_link.note: BTC next = BTC's move over the next 7 / 30 calendar days from the UTC day of the S&P close. Medians. Days in a state overlap, so the day counts are not independent cases; the early signs are counted once each. Since 1 Sep 2015. Past behaviour, not a forecast.
